format_paths.label: Shorts captured and edited on already owned phone
format_paths.limit: No mandatory dedicated purchased camera or software claimed; work, storage, connectivity and rights still matter

format_paths.label: Standard horizontal recorded video
format_paths.limit: Video editing, scripting, sound, accessibility and rights costs vary by project; 16:9 is not a paid-equipment mandate

format_paths.label: Webcam live stream
format_paths.limit: Uninterrupted network, moderation, preflight and post-live archive work matter

format_paths.label: Software or hardware encoded live stream
format_paths.limit: Capture/encoder setup, stream key control, ongoing network and monitoring effort can raise labor

format_paths.label: Complex live production
format_paths.limit: Multiple cameras/microphones/mixers are optional production choices, not YouTube-wide minimum spending

budget_levels.description: Use already-owned suitable hardware and no mandatory new purchase; record electricity, connectivity, licenses and labor separately.
Allocate fair use of existing camera/phone, microphone and computer using actual invoice and estimated useful life, with permission to reuse gear.
Optionally add equipment, software or contractor inputs only after a creator provides actual price and expected lifetime. No purchase recommendation.

matched_format_attempt_cost_protocol.estimator: Sum all attempted project labor/cash/gear allocations within each consented matched group. Divide by attempted count or published count separately; zero completions yield null rather than a finite per-published estimate.
limits: No unobserved unfinished or unpublished attempt may be dropped to create a low cost-per-video success estimate.
Paid contractor invoices belong to new cash paid; do not also add their working hours to the personal creator-hour total.
Owned equipment use allocations are noncash accounting costs and are not new equipment purchase invoices paid twice.
Both comparison groups must have a matching declared country, currency, topic, experience band and date frame.
Matching known fields does not remove creator self-selection; cannot attribute a difference causally to format.
Rates calculated on entered private or synthetic records cannot be published as a YouTube representative wage or median.
Comparing cost per published video requires counting all abandoned attempts' cash and labor in the group total.
Only a duly consented, documented sample can provide empirical descriptive estimates; no external account scraping is authorized.
